recap.workouts:
Three sessions, all three landed, and the day splits into a very good one and a worrying one.

06:00 Mechanical — 195 lb on the Enderton complex, the bottom of the band to the pound and exactly the call. Your rating a 5, and your own read was that total load on the body was fine but the squats were very hard. That is the complex doing its job. A three-second pause front squat plus a double-bounce plus a single at 80 percent is meant to be the hardest 195 you touch all week, and it is not the same 195 you took for pause triples on 18 August.

Leg day, maintenance dose, eight sets prescribed and eight sets landed:

belt squat 110 — 12/10
leg extension 100 — 12/12
leg curl 55 — 15/15
tibia raise 20 — 17/15

Both loads that were on trial came in at the ceiling of their range. Leg extension's first outing at 100 gave 12 and 12, the top of 8-12. Leg curl's first outing at 55 gave 15 and 15, the top of 12-15. Both stand, and both have already earned their next step. Your note about the new belt is the useful observation of the day: a bigger range of motion at the same number on the stack is more work, not less, so the 12 then 10 on the belt squat is the deeper position being paid for, not the load being wrong. 110 holds — and it was holding this week regardless.

CRe9 — and here the file and your note disagree completely, which is the whole story of the day.

The ride itself is close to flawless. 65 minutes on the clock, an average of 139 W against a Zone 1 band of 118-165, and 59 and a half of the 60 prescribed minutes genuinely inside Zone 1. Thirteen seconds of Zone X in the entire hour. Average heart rate 128 against a bike threshold of 159, peak 145, and the heart rate trend across the whole session is flat — no climb at all from the first minute to the last. The one instruction on this session was do not upgrade it to Zone 2 because it feels too easy, and you didn't. There is also a five-and-a-quarter-minute stretch carrying no data at about the point you describe, so the trace confirms the pause exactly where you put it.

And you were in a cold sweat and dizzy at 25 minutes. That is the finding of the day, and it is not a training finding. 139 W at 128 beats is the least your body was asked to do all week, on purpose. A session costing essentially nothing that produces those symptoms is telling you the cause is somewhere other than the session.
recap.takeaways:
1) THE RIDE WAS EXECUTED PERFECTLY, AND THAT IS EXACTLY WHY THE SYMPTOMS MATTER. Sixty minutes held inside Zone 1, thirteen seconds of Zone X, heart rate flat at 128 with a ceiling of 145 — fourteen beats under threshold. There is no fatigue signal anywhere in that trace, and nothing in it explains a cold sweat and dizziness. That is the useful part rather than the frustrating one: because the physiological cost was close to zero, the symptom cannot be read as the training being too much. It points somewhere else. You wrote "not completely recovered from illness" on 30 August and again on 1 September, and Monday's ride carried its own moment of feeling like fainting after the first set. Today is the second episode in three days. Confidence that this is not a training-load problem: high. Confidence about what it actually is: none — that is not a question this data can answer, and I am not going to pretend otherwise.

2) AND THE ONE THING I WILL PUSH BACK ON, PLAINLY. You wrote that the disappointment of not finishing would be worse than the physical risk of pushing through. On almost any other session I would be on your side of that — you know I would. Not this one. Dizziness and a cold sweat are the specific signal where stopping is the correct outcome rather than the failed one, and this was a Zone 1 hour, so there was no adaptation on the table worth the trade. Finishing it bought you nothing that the first 25 minutes had not already banked. If it turns up a third time, stop the session, and get it looked at by someone who can actually test for it. That has become a doctor's question rather than a coaching one, and asking it is not the same as backing off.

3) EIGHT SETS, TWO NEW LOADS, BOTH AT THE CEILING, AND BOTH TRIGGERED. Leg extension 100 and leg curl 55 were the last two applied bumps waiting to report, and they did not merely survive their first outing — they topped their ranges on it. That takes the week to five of the six banked bumps in and standing, with only Friday's pushdown superset at 105 left. Leg extension goes to 110 and leg curl to 60 on the next leg day. Belt squat holds at 110, and 120 still waits for the first leg day whose class morning is not a heavy squat day — that deferral has a named trigger and it has not fired.

4) ADAPT: NO-OP. All three of today's sessions classify as EXECUTED — the class at the called load, the lift at 8 of 8 sets, CRe9 at full duration inside the band. Nothing failed and nothing was skipped, so nothing in the remaining week moves, and I am not moving it on a symptom that the trace does not corroborate as load. Friday's RCI3 stands exactly as written. Its own first cut is already written into the plan if tomorrow asks for it, which is what the branch below is for — decided tonight rather than improvised at 06:00.
